name: Eye Defects-Arachnodactyly-Cardiopathy Syndrome
aliases: Eye Defects with Arachnodactyly and Cardiopathy

criteria.description: Presence of congenital eye defects such as microphthalmia or coloboma
Arachnodactyly characterized by abnormally long and slender fingers
Structural cardiac abnormalities including mitral valve prolapse or cardiomyopathy
Additional skeletal anomalies such as pectus excavatum or scoliosis
Distinctive facial features including high-arched palate and retrognathia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: congenital eye defects, arachnodactyly, and cardiopathy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by genetic testing when available.

pathognomonic.notes: Small, abnormally developed eyes present at birth
Long, slender fingers and toes resembling spider legs
Abnormal mitral valve function leading to regurgitation

common.symptomName: Coloboma of the iris or retina
common.notes: Defect in ocular tissue causing visual impairment
searchTerms: missing eye tissue in iris or retina

common.notes: Narrow and elevated roof of the mouth
Disease of the heart muscle affecting function

occasional.notes: Increased range of motion in joints
Reduced visual acuity due to ocular defects
Enlargement of the aortic root increasing risk of dissection
Slight delay in achieving developmental milestones

rare.notes: Separation of retina from underlying tissue
Impaired cardiac function leading to systemic symptoms
Collapsed lung due to air in pleural space
Life-threatening tear in the aortic wall

imaging: Echocardiogram showing mitral valve prolapse and cardiomyopathy
Chest X-ray revealing pectus excavatum or scoliosis
Ocular ultrasound or MRI demonstrating microphthalmia or coloboma
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible connective tissue disorder gene involvement
Genetic testing may exclude Marfan syndrome and related disorders
other: Clinical examination revealing arachnodactyly and facial dysmorphism

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of congenital eye malformations like coloboma
Distinctive craniofacial features absent in EDAC syndrome

redFlags: Progressive mitral valve prolapse with regurgitation
Sudden onset chest pain suggestive of aortic dissection
Severe visual impairment or retinal detachment
references: Pyeritz RE. Marfan syndrome: 25 years of research equals 25 years of additional life expectancy. Heart. 2019
